newsitem.title: USA: Moody's reviews Calif. debt in wake of Prop. 218.
newsitem.headline: Moody's reviews Calif. debt in wake of Prop. 218.

text.p: U.S. rating agency Moody's Investors Service Inc on Friday said it may downgrade $300 million of California Mello-Roos and assessment bonds, and planned to review $1.8 billion of outstanding debt following the passage of the state's controversial Proposition 218.

Moody's has so far affirmed eight outstanding Mello-Roos and assessment bonds, representing $425 million of debt, despite the California proposition, which limits the ability of local governments to raise taxes, the rating agency said in its Credit Perspectives newsletter.
Moody's said five ratings -- representing about $300 million of oustanding debt -- remain under review for possible downgrades because of Proposition 218.
"In addition, we are reviewing the underlying credit quality of all insured Mello-Roos and assessment bonds," representing about $1.8 billion of debt, Moody's said.

Proposition 218, which applies to all cities, counties, special districts, redevelopment agencies and school districts in the state, strengthened existing law to require that all new local taxes be submitted to voters for approval.

It also allows property owners to approve new assessments and strictly limits the use of fees and charges. Municipal analysts have warned that local governments may be required to reduce or repeal some existing property-related fees and assessments that do not meet the measure's restrictions.
Mello-Roos bonds are issued under the California's Mello-Roos Community Facilities Act of 1982.

The act allows local agencies to form community facilities districts that can issue bonds and levy special taxes to finance projects and services. More than 125 Mello-Roos districts have issued close to $3 billion of bonds since the act went into effect, according to a recent state report.
Moody's said the following ratings remain under review for possible downgrades:
* Los Alamitos USD special tax bonds, currently rated Baa1.
* Los Angeles County Flood Control District - Los Angeles County Public Works Financing Authority Capital Construction and Refunding Bonds, currently rated Aa1.
* Riverside County Flood Control and Water Conservation District - Elsinore Valley Benefit Assessment District bonds, currently rated single-A.
* Sacramento Area Flood Control Agency North Area Local Project Capital Assessment District No. 2 special assessment bonds, currently rated single-A.
* Y/S School Facilities Financing Authority special tax revenue series 1994 bonds, currently rated Baa1.
